title: Choose Snippi's visual world
question: The roll dealt The Key Cabinet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Key Cabinet
options.lineage: Grand-hotel front-desk key cabinets: walnut pigeonholes, brass hooks, enamel fobs
options.thesis: Every snippet hangs on its own hook; you take the key you need and go.
materials: enamel key fobs with stamped titles
ledger paper for the list view
options.viewport: The landing page is the cabinet face: a big grid of pigeonholes with real demo snippets on fobs. Headline and the sign-up button sit on the desk ledge below. Pick a fob and it swings off its hook, and its code opens beside the cabinet.
options.risk: If the wood and brass are rendered timidly it reads as a themed skin; it needs real joinery and fob physics to feel premium rather than kitsch.

raised.raise: One fob, one composition: each language gets its own enamel colour and stamped mark, so the library reads by colour at a glance.
Irreversible past a marked point: deleting is a staged return of the key to the desk, with a visible confirm, never a single click.
Real depth planes: cabinet back, hooks and fobs move at different scroll speeds, freezing flat under reduced motion.
The centre stays unmarked: the code area itself is never dressed in wood or brass; Monaco sits on a plain ground.

options.label: The Card Catalogue
options.lineage: Library card-catalogue drawers: oak, brass label frames, red-ruled index cards
options.thesis: Your library as a catalogue drawer: one card per snippet, filed and pulled in a second.
materials: buff index cards with a red header rule
options.viewport: One open drawer seen from above, cards fanned back, the front card set as the headline with the sign-up button on its tab.
options.risk: The most familiar of the grounded directions; paper and card stock drift toward the cream-and-serif look most generated sites land on.

options.label: ANSI Nightboard
options.lineage: Dial-up bulletin boards, ANSI art, sixteen colours
options.thesis: Snippi as a 2 a.m. BBS: your snippets are the file area and the title screen pours in at modem speed.
options.viewport: A block-art SNIPPI title screen streaming in line by line over a menu of file areas, fully keyboard driven.
options.case: Developers recognise it instantly, so it wins on audience; but monospace everywhere blurs the line between chrome and code, so it loses on clarity.
options.risk: Reads as retro novelty rather than premium, and an all-monospace screen fights the code it frames.

options.label: CD-ROM Console
options.thesis: A rendered console of embossed toggles with the code window as its one live area.
options.viewport: A fixed console frame with the Monaco editor in the central window and language toggles ranged around it.
options.case: The fixed console frames the editor clearly, so it holds on clarity; but few of today's developers grew up with it, so it loses on audience.
options.risk: Bevels and violet inlays tip into kitsch fast, and the fixed frame cramps phones.

options.label: Matchbook Drawer
options.thesis: Snippets as pocketable covers that flip open.
options.viewport: A fan of covers in hand.
options.risk: Nostalgia without a link to code.
options.case: Loses both axes: no developer link, and flips hide the code.
options.kept: One cover, one composition: each language gets its own fob colour and mark.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Snippets develop in stations under amber light.
options.viewport: A tray where the snippet image emerges.
options.risk: An amber wash ruins code legibility.
options.case: Loses both axes: slow staging fights a fast save-and-copy loop.
options.kept: Irreversible actions are staged past a marked point (delete).

options.label: Multiplane Dawn
options.thesis: Painted planes sliding through a forest morning.
options.viewport: A camera sinking through painted layers.
options.risk: Needs painted assets that don't exist; nothing to do with code.
options.kept: Real depth planes moving at different scroll speeds.

options.label: Accretion Threshold
options.viewport: A warped disk with labels orbiting the rim.
options.risk: Space spectacle is the dark-neon default in disguise.
options.kept: The centre stays unmarked: the code area carries no world material.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished dev-tool SaaS: neutral near-black, one accent, the product interface as the hero.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and sign-up button over a large crop of the real dashboard and editor.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other developer tool by design.
